core.title: Close every journey's continuation topology
core.given: A plan declares one or more journeys: each an entrypoint interlocking plus the interlockings reachable through continuations.
core.when: The plan reaches CONFIRM (always, for every declared journey, changed or not); also earlier whenever you author or change routes, continuations, terminals, entrypoints, or the trains those routes select.
core.then: Account for every reachable interlocking route exactly once: one continuation or one terminal, never both, never none.
prefer: Walk from the entrypoint, listing each (interlocking_id, route_id) with its one outgoing declaration.
Declare an explicit terminal for each route that ends the journey.
At CONFIRM, re-run the closure walk over every declared journey, not only the ones you edited.
avoid: Reusing a route_id inside one reachable interlocking; it must be unique.
Any continuation whose source route does not exist, whose artifact does not occur in the linear train that route selects, or whose destination interlocking does not exist; all three are mandatory.
Continuations or terminals on interlockings unreachable from the entrypoint; they are invalid.
Continuation cycles, even intended loops, until an explicit loop construct defines bounded/intentional repetition.
Implicit code-only handoffs or duplicate continuations.
core.why: Interlocking bilateral binding closes declaration→runtime→trace for one routing decision only; journey closure makes handoffs explicit, preventing silent gaps, duplicate continuations, disconnected fragments and artifact-free handoffs.
evidence: The journey closure check reports no findings for any declared journey at CONFIRM (confirm-blocking), including journeys unchanged by the current task.

Each finding identifies the journey, interlocking, route, artifact, destination interlocking and reason; a reviewer checks every reachable route maps to exactly one continuation or terminal, route_ids are unique per interlocking, and every continuation is anchored (source route, artifact in selected train, destination exist).
verification: Static closure check over the plan's declared journeys. Validation taxonomy: family closure; template graph_route_space_closure; variant planner_journey_continuation. Subject kind: journey; phase: CONFIRM; enforcement: confirm-blocking; applies to every journey subject at CONFIRM with no change prerequisite — including journeys unchanged by the current task.
route_key: each route is keyed by the pair (interlocking_id, route_id); route_id must be unique inside each reachable interlocking so the topology key is unambiguous.
accounted_route: a reachable route with exactly one outgoing declaration — continuation or terminal, never both.

Reachability is computed from the journey's entrypoint interlocking via continuation edges; continuation or terminal declarations whose source interlocking is unreachable from the entrypoint are invalid.

Continuation validity (all mandatory): the source route exists; the declared artifact occurs in the linear train selected by that route; the destination interlocking exists. artifact_handoff: the continuation artifact appears in the selected train's declared sequence, proving the cross-interlocking edge is anchored in the plan rather than invented by runtime code. Re-evaluate whenever route-to-train binding or train sequence changes.

acyclic_topology: continuation edges may not form a cycle in this version; continuation cycles are rejected until an explicit loop construct defines bounded/intentional repetition, so termination and proof obligations are not implicit.
Each finding reports the journey, interlocking, route, artifact, destination interlocking and reason for the failure.
Severity 4; disposition: strict — findings block CONFIRM; this rule declares no exception or waiver.

values: selected linear train sequence changed (artifact added/removed/renamed)

fires: Any task reaches CONFIRM on a plan that declares at least one journey, even if no journey, interlocking, route or train declaration changed in this task (every journey is re-checked).
A reachable interlocking route has neither a continuation nor a terminal, or has both.
A route is added to a reachable interlocking without a continuation or terminal.
Two routes inside one reachable interlocking share a route_id.
A continuation names an artifact that does not occur in the linear train its source route selects, including after the route is rebound to another train or the train's sequence is edited.
A continuation's source route or destination interlocking does not exist.
A continuation/terminal is declared for an interlocking unreachable from the journey entrypoint.
Continuations form a cycle between interlockings.
doesNotFire: Plans that declare no journeys at all (no journey subject to validate), even when they edit interlockings, routes or trains.

neutralityNotes: The whole convention lives in the ATDD plan model (journey, interlocking, route, continuation, terminal, linear train, CONFIRM phase), which is method-level rather than stack-level, so given/when/then/prefer/avoid/why/evidence and the activation situations carry over verbatim with no stack, runtime, language, path or suffix named. The validation taxonomy labels (family closure, template graph_route_space_closure, variant planner_journey_continuation) are stack-independent classifications of the check and are kept in core:verification, available to other realizations. The only realization specifics are this rule's concrete validator and finding identifiers (journeyContinuationFindings, planner.static.validators.bun), which per the notProfileKeys policy are bunOnly, while core:verification describes the check, its route_key/accounted_route/artifact_handoff/acyclic_topology semantics, its finding shape, and its severity-4 strict confirm-blocking disposition generically. No additional profile keys were needed beyond roles.plan_artifact.kinds, so proposedKeys is empty.
